seo.metaTitle: Pixelate PNG - Free Mosaic Filter, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Pixelate a PNG in your browser: every block is averaged into a single color, the classic mosaic effect. Choose the block size from 2 to 64 px. Free, no upload.
seo.longDescription: Pixelating an image hides detail by replacing every square block with one averaged color, which produces the blocky mosaic that covers faces, hides screens or simply reads as a retro effect. The block size slider runs from 2 to 64 pixels: small blocks give a fine grain, large blocks give an unmistakable mosaic. The dimensions of the picture do not change, so a pixelated result can still be used wherever the original size is expected. Like every tool here, it runs inside your browser - the file is never uploaded, and PNG, JPG, WebP and BMP are all accepted.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Set Block size to a small value for a fine grain or a large one for a heavy mosaic.
Watch the preview: each block becomes a single averaged color.
Save the result as PNG, JPG, WebP or BMP from the Download button.

faq.q: What block size should I pick?
faq.a: For covering a face, a block of roughly 1/20 to 1/12 of the smaller side works well - about 16 to 32 px on a 400 px image. Small images need small blocks: at 2 px the effect is a soft texture rather than a mosaic.

faq.q: Is pixelating the same as blurring?
faq.a: No. Blur averages neighbouring pixels smoothly, while pixelating replaces each block with one flat color and keeps hard square edges. That is what makes the result read as mosaic rather than as an out-of-focus picture.
Yes - move the block size back to the minimum or reload the original file. Nothing is destructive: the source image stays in the browser and the effect is re-applied on every change of the slider.

faq.q: Does it work with JPG and WebP, not only PNG?
faq.a: Yes. PNG, JPG, WebP and BMP are accepted on upload, and the pixelated result can be saved in any of them. A transparent PNG keeps its transparency after the blocks are averaged.
